name: Quadrantids
description: Sharp, short peak. Best after midnight; can produce bright fireballs.

name: Lyrids
description: One of the oldest recorded showers, with occasional bright fireballs.

name: Eta Aquariids
description: Fast meteors from Halley's Comet debris, best before dawn.

name: Southern Delta Aquariids
description: Steady Southern-Hemisphere shower; overlaps the early Perseids.

name: Perseids
description: The classic summer shower — bright, plentiful meteors on warm nights.

name: Orionids
description: Swift meteors from Halley's Comet, best in the hours before dawn.

name: Southern Taurids
description: Low rate but famous for slow, bright fireballs.

name: Northern Taurids
description: Fireball-rich stream that overlaps the Leonids.

name: Leonids
description: Fast meteors; historically capable of spectacular storms.

name: Geminids
description: The year's best shower: bright, slow, colorful meteors all night.

name: Ursids
description: A quiet northern shower close to the winter solstice.
